input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The guard uses all(...) instead of any(...) over the arguments' help attributes, so the section is gated on every argument being documented rather than on at least one.
- failure path: A command with arguments SRC (help set) and DST (no help) prints no 'Positional arguments' section at all in --help, silently dropping the documented text; conversely a command with zero arguments satisfies all([]) and prints an empty 'Positional arguments' header on every --help.

Reviewer finding
- description: The guard uses all() over the arguments, so the Positional arguments section is dropped whenever any single argument lacks help. The docstring says the section is written 'if at least one is documented', which would need any().
- rationale: Trigger: a command with two positional arguments, one with help text and one without. The check all(arg.help is not None ...) is False, so format_arguments writes nothing. Mechanism: the section is skipped entirely, even though the fallback in the list comprehension was added so that undocumented arguments still appear. Impact: users see no Positional arguments section at all for partially documented commands, which is the opposite of the commit's goal of listing every argument.
critique: The finding points to the same cause as the label: the guard uses all() where it should use any() over the arguments' help attributes. It also gives the same failure, where a partially documented command (one argument with help, one without) loses its whole Positional arguments section. It leaves out the empty-header case for zero arguments, but the core defect and mechanism are the same.
